title: PCA: finding the most informative direction
sub: Rotate a line through the cloud and project every point onto it.

frames.caption: 70 points with two correlated features. We want one number per point that keeps as much information as possible: project every point onto a line.
Direction 0°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 1.94.
Direction 15°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 2.43. Lost: the orange stems, the parts of each point the line can't represent.
Direction 30°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 2.66.
Direction 45°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 2.56.
Direction 60°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 2.15.
Direction 75°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 1.55.
Direction 90°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 0.92.
Direction 105°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 0.43.
Direction 120°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 0.20.
Direction 135°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 0.30.
Direction 150°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 0.70.
Direction 165°: the projections (orange) spread out with variance 1.30.

The best direction, 33°, is the top eigenvector of the covariance matrix: the first principal component. It keeps 93% of the total variance (2.67 of 2.86). Maximizing the variance kept is the same as minimizing the squared distances lost: variance kept + error = 2.86 always.
